newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar/yen seen up, but capped below 120 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/yen seen up, but capped below 120 yen.

text.p: The dollar is likely to edge higher against the yen on Wednesday, but a quick rise above the key resistance of 120 yen could be difficult due to selling by exporters and caution over remarks by monetary authorities.
"The dollar will cautiously test the upside today," said a dealer at a Japanese city bank.
If the dollar was able to pass 119.50 yen easily in early trade, it could rise as high as 119.70 yen, he said. "But a quick rise to 120 yen would seem to be difficult."
He said focus was on how much selling demand there would be on the way to the key psychological point of 120 yen.
The downside could be solid at around 118.80 due to the dollar's strong rally against the mark overnight and expectations of weak stocks and firmer yen bonds, dealers said.

A trust bank dealer said the dollar was likely to edge up against the yen as traders were expected to take profits on small rises. "I don't expect the dollar to jump quickly, but the downside could be limited at 118.80 yen," he added.

He said the market would watch the release of Japan's trade first 20 days trade data for July due out at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Tuesday). But he said attention had temporarily shifted away from trade issues to economic fundamentals.

Traders said they would watch out for remarks by Haruhiko Kuroda, the recently appointed director-general of the Japanese Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau at a meeting of the the Forex Club. Kuroda is expected to speak at the beginning of the meeting, which is scheduled to start around 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT), they said.
Dealers said the dollar could lack the energy to rise much against the mark in Asia after hitting a new 94-month high.
Mark buying-back against the dollar could prompt mark purchases against the yen, which could in turn help support the dollar against the yen, dealers said.
The Bundesbank surprised investors by fixing its repo rate at 3.0 percent for the next two weeks, despite predictions of a variable rate.

Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing also boosted the dollar with comments to German weekly magazine "Boerse-Online" indicating German officials were only worried about the speed of the dollar's strengthing, not its level.

"The dollar's bull-run against the mark could last and the Buba may not be able to halt the momentum unless it steps into the currency market to support the mark," the city bank dealer said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-1396
